---
title: "Constant Potential Molecular Dynamics in LAMMPS"
subtitle: "A practical guide to the ELECTRODE package"
---

## What Is This Guide?

This guide walks you through running **constant potential molecular dynamics (MD)** simulations using the [LAMMPS](https://lammps.org) ELECTRODE package. It is written for researchers and students who have a working LAMMPS installation and want to understand the physics behind the commands — not just the syntax.

## What You Will Learn

By the end of this guide you will be able to:

- **Interpret** LAMMPS input commands in terms of physical meaning
- **Connect** force field choices to simulation observables (energy, density, capacitance)
- **Design** electrode-electrolyte simulations with appropriate boundary conditions and physical parameters
- **Run** constant potential simulations and diagnose common problems
- **Analyze** output including trajectories, thermodynamic data, and electrode properties

## How to Use This Guide

The guide is organized as a sequence of topics, each building on the previous:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[1. Fundamentals] --> B[2. Force Fields]
    A --> C[4. Electrostatics]
    B --> C
    C --> D[5. Electrodes & CPM]
    D --> E[6. ELECTRODE Package]
    E --> F[7. Example]
    F --> G[8. Troubleshooting]
```

| Section | Topic | What You Will Understand |
|---------|-------|--------------------------|
| 1 | Fundamentals | What MD actually computes; key LAMMPS concepts |
| 2 | Force Fields | What interactions exist; how to configure them |
| 3 | Physical Conditions | How temperature, pressure, and time are controlled |
| 4 | Electrostatics | How long-range Coulomb is handled (Ewald, PPPM) |
| 5 | Electrodes & CPM | Why electrodes need special treatment; what CPM does |
| 6 | ELECTRODE Package | LAMMPS syntax for constant potential, charge, thermo |
| 7 | Example | A complete input script with output interpretation |
| 8 | Troubleshooting | Common problems and how to fix them |

## Prerequisites

This guide assumes you have:

- Completed introductory physics (mechanics, electromagnetism basics)
- Completed one semester of general chemistry (ions, Coulomb's law)
- Basic programming experience (any language)
- **Access to a LAMMPS installation** (binary or source; CMake-built with ELECTRODE and KSPACE packages)

No prior MD experience is required.

## Computing Environment

All examples in this guide assume a standard LAMMPS installation. Commands shown in `code blocks` like:

```{.bash}
lmp -in in.electrode -pk gpu 1 -l yes
```

should be run in a terminal where LAMMPS is available.
